items.title: Kimberly-Clark’s Dividend Is Up 392% Since 1999. Can Its $49 Billion Deal Put That at Risk?
items.summary: Kimberly-Clark has raised its payout for 54 straight years, yet last year's cash flow barely covered the check. With the Kenvue deal now closed and debt climbing, a few telltale signs will show whether the streak holds.

items.title: Kenvue (KVUE) Stock Still Looks Cheap Despite Its 27% Run
items.summary: Kenvue has delivered a 26.9% gain over the past year, and after a string of mixed but steady business updates, the key issue now is how much of that share price move is backed by the cash the company can generate over time. With the stock last closing at US$19.31 and a takeover by Kimberly-Clark progressing, investors are increasingly asking whether the current valuation still lines up with the underlying cash flows of the business. items.summary: Bond coupons never grow, but these four payers just handed shareholders a raise. One has a cash-rich balance sheet, one faces a $49 billion gamble, one is heading for a breakup, and one has a blemish on its record.

items.title: Her Brokerage Can Stop Reinvesting Dividends on Some Holdings and Send Her the Cash Instead. It’s a Setting Most Retirees Never Change
items.summary: Every quarter, dividends quietly buy shares you never planned to own while your checking account sits untouched. One overlooked brokerage setting changes that, but the tax rules and the compounding trade-off might surprise you.
